title: Mob lynching - is there a separate law or only general provisions
p1:
Mob lynching often makes headlines, but many people still ask: does India actually have a separate law for it?

The answer is more complex than a simple yes or no.
p2:
A common misconception is that every mob lynching case is handled under a special standalone law. In reality, there is no single central law titled “Mob Lynching Act” that covers all situations.

However, the law does recognize such crimes through specific provisions. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) includes a provision dealing with murder committed by a group of five or more persons acting together on certain grounds, while other offences may also apply depending on the facts of the case.
p3:
This means authorities can use criminal provisions based on what happened — such as murder, assault, unlawful assembly, or other relevant offences. The exact charge depends on the evidence and circumstances.

The key takeaway: mob lynching is not outside the law. It is addressed through existing criminal provisions, with some newer provisions specifically acknowledging group-based killings.
conclusion: Do you think India needs a separate comprehensive law for mob lynching, or are existing criminal provisions enough?
